oil.when: 2010–2011 with the message center and the SETUP and RESET buttons
steps: Reset only after the oil and filter have actually been changed.
Turn the ignition to ON. The engine does not need to be running.
Press and release SETUP until the message center shows OIL LIFE XXX% HOLD RESET = NEW.
Press and hold RESET for about two seconds, then let go. Oil life goes back to 100%.
oil.note: If you keep tapping RESET while OIL LIFE SET TO XXX% is showing, each tap lowers the starting value by 10%. Leave it at 100% unless your service shop told you otherwise.

The 2009 owner guide lists the message center menus and warnings with no oil life item or oil change message, so there is no oil reminder to reset. Change the oil by the mileage schedule in the owner guide.

tpms.when: 2010–2011 (sensor in each road wheel, no reset button)
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressure on the sticker in the driver's door opening.
Drive above 20 mph for at least two minutes.
The light goes out on its own once the system reads good pressures. There is no reset button or menu for it.
If the tires are set correctly, the spare is not on the car, and the light stays on or flashes, have the system checked soon.
tpms.note: If the light flashes for about a minute at start-up and then stays on, that is a system fault, and adding air or driving will not clear it. The temporary spare has no sensor, so the light stays on while the spare is fitted.

notes: The Milan is a twin of the Ford Fusion of the same years, and the reminders work the same way.
